articles.title_orig: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk Says He Will Give a SpaceX Share to ‘Every Kid in America’
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, the world's richest person, pledged Monday to give each child in the U.S. one of his SpaceX shares.
Elon Musk has pledged to give every child in America one share of SpaceX next year, signaling that the planned giveaway could be the first of several.
"Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," he wrote in a Monday post on X.
The pledge followed an exchange with artificial intelligence company Anthropic over its plans to dedicate a portion of its equity to public benefit initiatives.
TESLA'S NEW ROADSTER MAKES A FLYING DEBUT, HITTING 60 MPH IN UNDER A SECOND
Elon Musk speaks during the World Economic Forum (WEF) annual meeting in Davos on January 22, 2026. (Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP via Getty Images / Getty Images)
On Sunday, Musk urged Anthropic to distribute shares directly to the public after the company outlined its plans for the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund.
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk receives the National Medal of Science from U.S. President Donald Trump during the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit at the Institute of Peace on Oct. 8, 2026, in Washington, D.C. ( Win McNamee/Getty Images / Getty Images)
"We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit. It will start off with 5% of our shares. For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion. In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good," Anthropic noted in a Sunday post on X.
"Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding," the company added.
Anthropic Co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei arrives at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on Sept. 29, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images / Getty Images)
Responding to Anthropic's announcement, Musk wrote, "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public."
He then indicated that he intended to follow that approach himself.
"This is what I will be doing," he added in another post.

Musk followed up Monday with his pledge to distribute SpaceX shares to American children, although he did not provide details about how the proposed giveaway would work.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Rebounds at Open After Friday's Tech Selloff — Live Updates
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Nasdaq Rebounds at Open After Friday's Tech Selloff — Live Updates
articles.content_orig:
U.S. stock futures rose slightly on Monday night, following a mostly higher session on Wall Street as investors jumped back into tech names after a fierce sell-off last week.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded 56 points higher, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.1% along with Nasdaq-100 futures .
The S&P 500 climbed 0.4% in regular trading, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced more than 1%, with tech leading the charge. Nvidia added 1.4%, and Tesla jumped 3.8%. Alphabet shares advanced about 1%.
Tech last week suffered a rout that spilled over into the broader market, as concerns grew around companies borrowing too much money for their artificial intelligence build-outs.
"Improving moods regarding the prospects of modern technology have Wall Street breathing a sigh of relief as participants drop hedges, after the cost of volatility protection soared intraday on Friday, ahead of the intensifying selloff," wrote Jose Torres, senior economist at Interactive Brokers.
CoreWeave , which fell more than 25% last week, tried to recover some of that decline after a Goldman Sachs upgrade to buy. However, early gains fizzled and the stock closed slightly lower.
Investors on Tuesday will parse through a slew of corporate earnings. United Airlines is due to post after the bell, while General Motors is set to report before the open.
It's a busy week of earnings, with roughly 70 S&P 500 companies on deck to report results. Housing starts and pending home sales figures are also scheduled for release Tuesday.
AI stocks rallied on Monday, but CoreWeave closed slightly lower as investors remained skittish about its debt. Yields on Oracle debt also remained elevated as credit worries persist across the AI trade.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 1% on Monday. CoreWeave , the so-called neocloud company that led the sell-off last week, bounced around, hit a 52-week low and ultimately closed fractionally lower. Meanwhile, its bond yields remained high and its five-year credit default swaps were at distressed levels.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded 56 points higher, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.1%. Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.2%.

Teams from the National Migration Institute, working with police and intelligence officers, interviewed 86 Chinese citizens at 54 shops in Comayaguela, Tegucigalpa’s twin city and main commercial district, and told 25 of them to report for further document checks.
Migration officers also went to Choluteca, in the south, where China’s SFECO Group is building a regional hospital, and found that 16 of the 128 Chinese workers on site were in an irregular situation.
